When the global 'pool dirty' byte is set it rebuilds the shared pool of 0x1C-byte records (zeroed, class descriptor 0x007F52B8 installed, stored through *0x007BE300) and clears the flag; it then reads the input state and the save bytes at bag+0x985C / bag+0x2CFD and pushes the next sub-state ids (6, 0xB, 0xC..0x18) onto the state vector at self+0x3B8.

The disassembly (0x00304900..0x00304D44) shows the lazy 0x1C-byte-record pool rebuild behind a global flag byte and the std_InlinedVector16_PushByte calls on self+0x3B8. The 0x24A98 in the disassembly is only the save-work base the function reads two flag bytes from (bag+0x985C and bag+0x2CFD); there is no Item_LookupRecord call and no item-id range anywhere in it, so this is not item code despite the 'Text' in the name.

name: Ui_TwoPaneWindow_ApplyCursorMoveRequest
summary: Vtable slot 0 of the two-pane window class (vtable 0x0076317C, next to Ui_Window_LayoutRows and Ui_TwoPaneWindow_ShowSecondPane): ticks the active child widget with child->vt[+0x2C](child, 1.0f) and, when the pending cursor-move record at self+0x184 is marked visible (byte +0x14 bit 0) and the window flag +0x14C is set, moves the cursor of the pane at self+0x138 by the record's signed deltas (+0x16 dx, +0x17 dy, +0x18 wrap) through 0x001A60A0, which forwards to Ui_Cursor_Move.

The old name claimed a visibility update, but the body only reads the visibility bit and moves a cursor.
